pr.title: Show a loop's open pull requests in a Claude Code pane
pr.head: 742c9234d60867e8d182553eca151b58dc4236ef

summary: Projector's fix and review loops each run a watcher script in the background: watch-prs.sh for a review loop and watch-threads.sh for a fix loop. Each watcher reads a tracked file, a plain text file with one owner/repo#number line for each pull request the loop owns. Until now, to see which pull requests a loop watches and which of them need work, you read that file and looked each pull request up on GitHub.

This pull request adds a Claude Code hooks module: TypeScript that Claude Code loads from a plugin's hooks/ directory and runs on engine events, such as a tool call or a slash command. The module draws a pane, titled Loop PRs, that lists each loop's open pull requests. Each row shows a link, draft or ready, and the title. A second line appears when the pull request has a merge conflict, a change request, or unresolved review threads.

• How the pane finds loops. When the session runs a watcher through the Bash or Monitor tool, the module reads the command's --tracked argument and opens the pane. It also scans ps for watchers that other sessions started. /loop-prs <file> adds a tracked file by hand.
  • How it asks GitHub. One gh api graphql call each minute fetches every listed pull request, and only while the pane is open. Press r to refresh at once.
  • What it leaves alone. The module is Claude Code packaging only. No skill depends on it, and Codex gets nothing new.
The validation gate gains claude plugin test ., which runs the module's *.test.ts files.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Watcher: the shell script a loop runs in the background, watch-prs.sh or watch-threads.sh.
  • Tracked file: the file a watcher reads, one owner/repo#number per line. A !owner/repo#number line keeps that pull request out.
  • Hooks module: a plugin's TypeScript that Claude Code runs on engine events.
  • Pane: a framed region of the Claude Code screen that a plugin draws.

groups.title: Packaging the hooks module for Claude Code only
groups.kicker: Where Claude Code finds the module, and the state it keeps
intro: Claude Code finds hooks/hooks.json at the plugin root by itself, and that file names the module's entry point, register.tsx. The Claude manifest adds a types field that points at hooks/types.d.ts, the module's state contract. That file declares the two values the module keeps in plugin state: the loops the session has seen, and the last snapshot it drew.
The Codex manifest does not change, and a new packaging test checks that it names neither types nor hooks.

files.note: Adds types, pointing at the module's state contract.
Names register.tsx as the module Claude Code loads.
The pull request, loop, and snapshot shapes, and the projector plugin-state keys seenLoops and loopSnapshot.
Checks that the module and its contract exist, and that only the Claude manifest declares them.

groups.title: Reading watcher commands and tracked files
groups.kicker: Pure functions that find a watcher's tracked path and read the file
intro: The module learns a loop from a shell command, either the one the session ran or a line of ps output. tokenize splits the command into words and operators, and it records which parts of each word were quoted. findWatchers looks for a word whose last path segment is watch-prs.sh or watch-threads.sh. It then reads that command's --tracked value and stops at the next operator, such as ; or &&.

expand expands a leading ~ and $NAME outside single quotes, using only the environment. It gives up on a command substitution or an unknown variable, so the caller can tell the person to add the file by hand. parseTracked reads the tracked file with the same entry pattern the watchers use.

files.note: The tokenizer, path expansion, watcher detection, and tracked-file parser.

checks.text: Open finding: expand reads variables only from the environment. A loop started as D=~/.local/state/projector; ID=…; bash …/watch-prs.sh --tracked $D/$ID.tracked, the form this machine's own loops use, gets tracked: undefined. The session then gets a toast asking it to add the file by hand, and the ps scan lists the loop under "another session". The fix is to read NAME=value words that come earlier in the same command.
parseTracked matches ! exclusions and duplicates with case. parse_tracked in watch-prs.sh ignores case, so a differently cased ! line can leave a pull request in the pane that the watcher drops.

files.note: Covers watcher detection, expansion, the tracked-file parser, and the GitHub query and response.

groups.title: Asking GitHub for every pull request at once
groups.kicker: One GraphQL query, and a reader that tolerates a missing pull request
intro: buildQuery groups the pull requests by repository and gives each one an alias, so one gh api graphql call fetches all of them. Repository names come from parseTracked, which admits only the characters GitHub allows in a name, so they are safe inside the query's string literals.
parseResponse keeps whatever data came back. A pull request that does not exist leaves its slot null and adds an error, but the call fails only when no data came back at all.

files.note: Builds the query and reads its answer into PullRequest records.

checks.text: reviewThreads(first: 100) reads only the first 100 threads, so the open-thread count is too low on a pull request with more.

groups.title: The hooks and the pane
groups.kicker: Learning loops from tool calls, polling GitHub, and drawing the pane
intro: register.tsx wires the module to Claude Code events:

• session.start registers /loop-prs and starts a one-minute timer. The timer refreshes only while the pane is open.
  • tool.call for Bash and Monitor lets the tool run first. When the command started a watcher, the hook records the tracked file and opens the pane. A .catch handler replays the tool's result, so a failure in the hook never runs the tool twice.
  • command.run for /loop-prs records a tracked file given as an argument, then opens the pane.
  • ui.render for the pane draws the last snapshot. It shows open pull requests, a count of merged or closed ones, and entries GitHub could not find.

load merges the session's own loops with watchers that ps found, reads each tracked file, and makes one GitHub call for every pull request. When that call fails, the pane keeps what GitHub returned last time.

files.note: The event hooks, the refresh loop, and the pane's drawing.

checks.text: Open finding: adopt returns true for every watcher command, even one whose tracked file the session already holds, so each run calls show. A loop under Monitor starts its watcher again at least every 30 minutes, so a pane you closed opens again each time. The fix is to open the pane only when adopt adds a new loop.
A forced refresh that starts while another refresh runs gets that run's result. A loop added during the run appears at the next poll, up to a minute later.

files.note: Drives a watcher command through tool.call, answers ps, file reads, and gh from memory, and checks what the pane draws.
